name: Deep-sinking carbon bloom
subtitle: algae bred to carry carbon downward

effects.effect: a cell can run on a genome written entirely by computer
plants turn sunlight, water and carbon dioxide into sugar

effect: a cell can run on a genome written entirely by computer
how: Ocean algae pull down huge amounts of carbon each year, but almost all of it is eaten and breathed back out within weeks near the surface. Algae built to make heavy, indigestible shells at the end of their short lives would sink quickly instead, carrying their carbon below the depth where it comes back for centuries. Satellites already watch bloom colour, so the amount sunk could in principle be checked from orbit.
obstacle: Nobody can yet verify how much carbon actually reaches the deep, and seeding engineered life in international waters has no legal owner.
why: Export efficiency and governance, not biology, are what stop this.
real: An EBRC roadmap case study proposes releasing engineered algae with increased carbon capture and sinking biomass, and ballasted-particle export (Gigablue, mineral ballast studies) is being measured, but no organism engineered to make heavy indigestible shells for carbon export was found.
